insights.title: Your blood sugar results are in the diabetes range
insights.found: HbA1c 8.4% and fasting glucose 172 mg/dL (9.5 mmol/L) on 5 Oct 2026. You take metformin and glimepiride.
insights.why: Both are above the diabetes-range criteria our rules use.
insights.means: Our rules are written for diagnosis, so they ask for confirmation and a check that HbA1c is reliable (no haemoglobin variant, recent transfusion or red-cell breakdown). For someone already on treatment, what matters is your target and the trend.
insights.do: Ask your doctor what HbA1c target suits you and when to repeat it; our analysis window for a repeat is within 3 months.
insights.expected: A repeat shows whether your current treatment is working.

insights.title: Your urine shows albumin, and your eGFR may be overestimated
insights.found: Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 64 mg/g (lab limit: below 30) and eGFR 67 on 5 Oct 2026.
insights.why: eGFR is in the 60-89 band, and in Indian cohorts creatinine-based equations overestimate true kidney function.
insights.means: Your true kidney function may be lower than 67. The albumin in your urine is above the lab's limit; no rule in our library graded it on its own.
insights.do: Ask about cystatin C, a second kidney marker, and a repeat urine albumin test.
insights.expected: Two kidney markers and a repeat urine test give a truer picture.

insights.title: Your waist, weight and HDL add up to a metabolic-risk pattern
insights.found: Waist 94 cm, BMI 29.1 and HDL cholesterol 44 mg/dL on 5 Oct 2026.
insights.why: Waist is above the Asian-Indian cut-point for women (80 cm), BMI is above the WHO Asian action point (23), and HDL is below 50, one of five metabolic-syndrome factors.
insights.means: Together with high triglycerides and blood sugar, this is the metabolic-syndrome pattern our rules recognise. The BMI finding is informational and is not a label of obesity.
insights.do: Talk with your doctor about the changes that suit you; waist is rechecked in 6 to 12 months.
insights.expected: A smaller waist usually moves several of these numbers together.

insights.title: Your triglycerides are high on one fasting test
insights.why: Our rule flags 175 mg/dL or more.
insights.means: A lasting rise is a risk-enhancing factor in the 2018 AHA/ACC guideline. One value cannot show it is lasting; a second fasting value can.
insights.do: Repeat a fasting lipid test within 2 weeks to 3 months.
insights.expected: A second value shows whether this is persistent.

insights.title: One liver enzyme is above the healthy range for South Indian women
insights.why: It is above 24 U/L, the 97.5th percentile of healthy South Indian women, though within many labs' printed range.
insights.means: Our rule reads this together with a liver-scarring score (FIB-4) and proposes no test on its own.
insights.do: Mention it to your doctor with your other results.
insights.expected: Your doctor decides whether a FIB-4 score is needed.

ask.q: What does my HbA1c of 8.4 mean?
ask.a: HbA1c is your average blood sugar over the last 2-3 months. 8.4% is in the diabetes range, with fasting glucose 172 mg/dL on the same day. Ask your doctor what target suits you; our analysis suggests repeating it within 3 months.
Your results from 5 Oct 2026 are above the diabetes-range criteria while you take metformin and glimepiride. Only your doctor can set your target, and a repeat HbA1c shows the trend.

Your eGFR was 67, and in Indian cohorts this equation tends to overestimate kidney function. Your urine albumin was 64 mg/g, above the lab's limit of 30. A repeat urine test and cystatin C would give a truer picture.

ask.q: Is my cholesterol OK on atorvastatin?
ask.a: On 5 Oct 2026: LDL 118 mg/dL (flagged high by the lab), HDL 44 (low for women) and triglycerides 190 (high). The triglyceride result needs a second fasting test to show it is lasting. Your doctor reviews these against your statin.
Your waist was 94 cm, above the 80 cm cut-point for Asian-Indian women, and your BMI was 29.1. With low HDL, high triglycerides and high blood sugar, it forms the metabolic-syndrome pattern.
ALT was 30 U/L, slightly above the healthy range for South Indian women (24). Our rule reads it with a liver-scarring score and proposes no test on its own.
Your systolic was 138 mmHg, flagged high by the lab but below our rule's 140 threshold. A repeat pair of readings at your panel visit shows the trend.
Not calculated. PhenoAge needs nine blood results; 7 are missing: albumin, CRP, lymphocyte %, MCV, RDW, alkaline phosphatase and white cell count.
Not calculated. The PREVENT model needs total cholesterol, smoking status, BMI and whether you are treated for blood pressure, and the run did not have them all. We never fill gaps with guesses.

ask.q: What did the drug discovery research find?
ask.a: It found 25 biological targets (the portal lists the first 12) linked to your record, including blood-sugar genes such as GLP1R, DPP4 and SLC5A2, and profiled 730 known compounds. No docking was run. Research only, not treatment.

glossary: HbA1c
Average blood sugar over about the last 2-3 months.
Fasting glucose
Blood sugar after not eating for 8 hours or more.
UACR
Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio: how much protein (albumin) leaks into the urine.
eGFR
Estimated glomerular filtration rate: how well your kidneys filter, calculated from creatinine, age and sex.
LDL / HDL
Two kinds of cholesterol in the blood. LDL is the main one linked to clogged arteries; HDL is often called 'good' cholesterol.
Triglycerides
A type of fat in the blood, measured after fasting.
Waist
Waist circumference: a measure of fat around the middle.
BMI
Body mass index: weight divided by height squared.
ALT
Alanine aminotransferase: a liver enzyme measured in blood.
Rule
One of our clinical checks. Each has a source, a threshold and an evidence grade; it fires only when your result clears it.

genes.function: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork together with laminins, proteoglycans and entactin/nidogen.
PPIase that catalyzes the cis-trans isomerization of proline imidic peptide bonds in oligopeptides and may therefore assist protein folding.

Metabolic-stress sensing protein kinase that phosphorylates the alpha subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (EIF2S1/eIF-2-alpha) in response to various stress, such as unfolded protein response (UPR).
Deacetylates a wide range of non-histone substrates.
Electrogenic Na(+)-coupled sugar symporter that actively transports D-glucose at the plasma membrane, with a Na(+) to sugar coupling ratio of 1:1.
Receptor for both mineralocorticoids (MC) such as aldosterone and glucocorticoids (GC) such as corticosterone or cortisol.
Receptor for angiotensin II, a vasoconstricting peptide, which acts as a key regulator of blood pressure and sodium retention by the kidney.
G protein-coupled receptor for glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1).
Cell surface glycoprotein receptor involved in the costimulatory signal essential for T-cell receptor (TCR)-mediated T-cell activation.
